corpusSummary: Across 2026 social-science studies, large language models are analyzed as tools, agents, and social actors. The corpus reveals four recurring trajectories: (1) leveraging LLMs as research tools with attention to validation, bias, and ethics; (2) exploring human-AI interaction, trust, embodiment, and adoption in education, counseling, and daily life; (3) health, governance, and literacy challenges around AI-mediated information; (4) concerns about bias, misinformation, and reliability in AI systems and discourse.

themes.name: AI as a research tool and methodological practice
themes.description: A growing set of papers treat LLMs as research tools—data extraction, coding, cross-domain analysis, and simulations—while calling for rigorous validation, transparency, and ethical safeguards.

themes.name: Human–AI interaction, trust, adoption, and embodiment
themes.description: Research on human-AI interaction spans trust, adoption, embodiment, and presenting formats across counseling, education, work, and everyday use, including device embodiment and social-capital dynamics.

themes.name: AI in health, education, and governance with equity and safety
themes.description: Work examines AI’s use in health, education, and public governance, foregrounding safety, equity, AI literacy, and responsible design in AI-mediated communication and decision making.

themes.name: Bias, misinformation, and reliability in AI systems
themes.description: A substantial thread centers on bias, misinformation, fallibility, and reliability of LLMs and AI systems, with studies on deception, warnings, persuasion, and correctability.
